paragraphs: D2L sells Brightspace, a learning platform that holds course design, assessments, analytics and AI features in one system. It is marketed first to colleges and universities. The company also pitches it to K-12 districts. A public sector version is offered for agencies with regulatory and security requirements.

Instructors build assessments, align them to outcomes and track learner progress as it happens. Reporting centralizes data so an institution can measure enrollment, engagement, retention and completion. The platform raises early warning signals so faculty can reach students who are falling behind. AI features come through D2L Lumi, which the company says is made for education rather than general use. It states that customer data is not used to train that model.

The higher education page cites more than 1,300 customers. The company claims more than 25 years of education technology work behind Lumi. Purdue University is described as consolidating its teaching tools onto Brightspace. For public sector buyers the site notes a partnership with Carahsoft.

quote.text: Stop stitching tools together. Brightspace keeps course design, assessments, analytics and AI all in one place, so intelligence shows up where the work is already happening.
